bounds.domain: Three request handlers, two stop callers, at most three accepted normal-priority items, one drain owner, one repeat task and at most one storage startup failure. Marker checks, startup settlement and queue retirement are separate actions.
assumptions: A failed startup clears both cached owners. Only a later accepted request triggers another start; no autonomous retry is assumed or claimed. RetryRestoresDrain applies only after that later request actually starts the retry.

Fairness assumes enabled marker checks and storage-start attempts settle, a second storage attempt succeeds after the one allowed failure, the existing scheduler serves ready drain work, and disposal completes. Without that fairness, RetryWithoutFairness must produce a loop counterexample.

Stop retires admission before awaiting startup and repeated stop joins the existing cleanup. Successful disposal is assumed for StopSettles; failed cleanup, partial high-priority flush and failed durable task-row deletion are outside this projection. Already-accepted normal-priority work may be explicitly discarded during fast shutdown. Processing represents a terminal queue outcome, not proof of correct PII redaction, model completion, high-priority flush behavior or unbounded queue progress. The real PGlite hook checks task startup failure/retry and stop ownership; it does not enumerate every model schedule.

Fairness assumes enabled startup settles, disposal completes successfully, and each waiting stop caller observes its shared cleanup completion. A second stop joins the existing operation and cannot return success before queue cleanup completes. Cleanup failure and partial disposal remain outside this projection.
No fairness is assumed. An enabled response, storage settlement, drain or polling action may stutter forever; a temporal loop counterexample is required.

Storage settlement, ready drain, marker-check and disposal actions are weakly fair, as in Fairness. No later request is assumed. After a failed start, queued work can remain with no task; fairness alone does not trigger another start. A temporal loop counterexample is required.
